evidence.title: Unknown-to-known availability correction is suppressed at archive admission before point-in-time revision selection
evidence.proof_level: Exact-SHA source inspection and deterministic regression oracle only; NOT full repository pytest or observed incident
source_chain: contracts.py FlowObservation.observation_id includes available_at_ms and observed_at_ms, so two records differing only in availability/observation clocks have different IDs; visible_at rejects available_at_ms=None.

storage.py append_observations builds latest_signature by revision_key, then skips new IDs when _semantic_signature equals prior signature. _semantic_signature omits available_at_ms and observed_at_ms.

Therefore first archive row available_at_ms=None followed by same economic row with known available_at_ms and later observed_at_ms can be skipped even though the latter becomes PIT eligible. Reverse input order retains the known row.

runner.py run_once external_jsonl collection -> append_observations -> load_observations -> _scoring_history -> engine/handoff/health. Collector OK counts do not prove admission of corrected availability.

Existing test_providers_replay.py test_archive_skips_unchanged_reobservation_but_keeps_real_revision intentionally skips reobserved unchanged economic values but does not test unknown-to-known availability. Normalization's test_later_available_correction_wins does not exercise archive admission.
evidence.distinct_from_C: A concerns durable archive admission before normalization. C's equal-rank, future-effective dedup and handoff issues occur after admission.
